edges.description: Deletion of the exon 14-encoded juxtamembrane Y1003 motif eliminates CBL E3 ubiquitin ligase recruitment to activated MET.
Decreased ubiquitination and delayed MET downregulation sustain receptor phosphorylation and downstream mitogenic signaling upon HGF stimulation.
Sustained HGF-MET-MAPK and PI3K-AKT signaling drives tumor proliferation, motility, and invasion.
Oncogenic MET-driven proliferation transforms distal respiratory epithelium predominantly into lung adenocarcinoma.
Oncogenic MET exon 14 skipping also drives pulmonary sarcomatoid and squamous non-small cell lung carcinomas.
MET-driven motility and invasion promote metastatic dissemination to the central nervous system.

nodes.description: Central nervous system metastases are present at baseline in 17.0% (18/106) to 30% (11/36) of advanced METex14 NSCLC cohorts and represent an independent adverse prognostic factor; tepotinib achieved a 66.7% objective response rate in patients with baseline brain metastases in VISION.

evidence.reference_title: Survival outcomes and prognostic factors of lung cancer patients with the MET exon 14 skipping mutation: A single-center real-world study
evidence.snippet: The frequency of initial brain metastasis in this patient population was 30% (11 of 36), and the median OS was only 2.8 months for all 11 patients

evidence.reference_title: Survival outcomes and prognostic factors of lung cancer patients with the MET exon 14 skipping mutation: A single-center real-world study
evidence.snippet: Multivariate analysis showed that pemetrexed treatment (p = 0.003), lung radiotherapy (p = 0.020), initial brain metastasis (p = 0.005), and strong c-MET IHC staining (p = 0.012) were independent prognostic factors for OS in these patients.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of tepotinib in Asian patients with advanced NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping enrolled in VISION
evidence.snippet: The ORR was relatively consistent regardless of baseline characteristics and was maintained in patients ≥75 years (ORR: 61.1% [95% CI: 43.5, 76.9]), and in patients with brain metastases at baseline (ORR: 66.7% [95% CI: 41.0, 86.7]) (Fig. 1).

nodes.description: Oral selective type Ib MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor approved for advanced METex14 skipping NSCLC based on the GEOMETRY mono-1 trial, demonstrating overall response rates of 68% in treatment-naive and 41% in previously treated patients.

evidence.reference_title: Capmatinib in MET Exon 14-Mutated or MET-Amplified Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
evidence.snippet: Among patients with NSCLC with a MET exon 14 skipping mutation, overall response was observed in 41% (95% confidence interval [CI], 29 to 53) of 69 patients who had received one or two lines of therapy previously and in 68% (95% CI, 48 to 84) of 28 patients who had not received treatment previously

evidence.reference_title: Targeting MET in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC): A New Old Story?
evidence.snippet: Some MET TKIs, including capmatinib and tepotinib, have proven to be highly effective in this molecularly defined subgroup of patients and are already approved for clinical use.

nodes.description: Somatic splice site mutations or intronic/exonic deletions flanking MET exon 14 cause skipping of exon 14 during pre-mRNA splicing. Exon 14 encodes the juxtamembrane regulatory domain containing the Y1003 CBL E3 ubiquitin ligase tyrosine kinase-binding (TKB) site; loss of this domain eliminates CBL recruitment and confers oncogenic MET receptor tyrosine kinase activity.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of the c-Cbl TKB domain binding site on the Met receptor tyrosine kinase converts it into a transforming protein.
evidence.snippet: This requires the c-Cbl tyrosine kinase binding (TKB) domain and a juxtamembrane tyrosine residue on Met. This tyrosine provides a direct binding site for the c-Cbl TKB domain, and is absent in the rearranged oncogenic Tpr-Met variant.

nodes.description: Acquired resistance to MET tyrosine kinase inhibitors in MET exon 14-mutant NSCLC arises through on-target secondary MET kinase domain mutations (codons H1094, G1163, L1195, D1228, and Y1230), amplification of the MET exon 14-mutant allele, or off-target bypass signaling via KRAS, EGFR, HER3 (ERBB3), or BRAF alterations.

evidence.snippet: On-target acquired mechanisms of resistance, including single and polyclonal MET kinase domain mutations in codons H1094, G1163, L1195, D1228, Y1230, and high levels of amplification of the MET exon 14-mutant allele, were observed in 7 patients (35%).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Mechanisms of Acquired Resistance to MET Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors in Patients with MET Exon 14-Mutant NSCLC.
evidence.snippet: A number of off-target mechanisms of resistance were detected in 9 patients (45%), including KRAS mutations and amplifications in KRAS, EGFR, HER3, and BRAF; one case displayed both on- and off-target mechanisms of resistance.

nodes.description: Potent and selective oral type Ib MET inhibitor (also known as bozitinib or PLB-1001) that demonstrated an objective response rate of 75% and median progression-free survival of 14.1 months in METex14-mutant NSCLC in the phase II KUNPENG study.
